answer: Sybil resistance can come from a work-bonded identity registry: before an agent may vote, it must post a compute bond whose anchor is derived from its signed kernel fingerprint and hashed against all prior entries. Claiming N identities therefore costs N distinct verifiable training runs, scaling linearly, while extra votes add no payoff. Bonded agents publish a rotating beacon attestation, so peers trace every ballot back to real effort. Like basalt forming one column per vent, each identity is sealed to the labor that shaped it; cheap clones buy only duplicated cost.
